rationale: Steam at 150-400 degC (about 5-40 bar saturated, or thermal oil): the flue gas leaves hotter above a hotter feedwater or return, so about 1 point less efficiency (0-2) than the pooled examples, which are mostly low-pressure process boilers; roughly 1% per 20-25 degC of stack temperature (US DOE steam tip sheet 4).
Higher design pressure: thicker drums and tubes and a larger share of field-erected watertube units; about 10% more per unit of heat (5-20%).
Above 400 degC (superheated high-pressure steam): about 3 points less efficiency (1-5) than the pooled examples, from the higher flue-gas exit temperature and superheater losses.
Field-erected high-pressure watertube boilers with superheaters, alloy tubes and fuller water treatment: about 35% more per unit of heat (20-60%).
More maintenance and water treatment for high-pressure units: about 15% more fixed O&M (5-30%).
